items.job: Diagnose airbag light and repair under-seat connectors or replace failed sensor
items.note: Owners report about $160 for a harness and $250 for a sensor; a clock-spring or airbag module costs much more.

items.t: Side airbag wiring under seat can come loose (recall)
Engine can stall from engine computer defect (recall)
Wrong tire pressure label on door (recall)
Fuel tank valve may leak in a rollover (recall)
Gas pump keeps clicking off or fuel spits back
items.job: Diagnose and repair fuel filler neck or tank vent (EVAP) parts
items.note: One owner spent over $300 without a fix, so insist on a diagnosis first.

items.t: Engine surges or car lunges forward
items.job: Diagnose throttle and idle control system
items.note: RepairPal lists about $122-$179 for diagnosis. Parts such as a throttle sensor cost extra.

items.t: Check engine light from throttle or accelerator pedal sensor
items.job: Replace throttle position sensor and relearn throttle
items.note: RepairPal lists about $345-$667; one owner paid about $300.

items.t: Check engine light for lean codes P0171 / P0174
items.job: Smoke-test intake and repair vacuum leak
items.note: Cost depends on what is leaking; an intake gasket job costs more.

items.t: Rough idle from faulty EGR switching valve
items.note: YourMechanic averages about $62 in parts and $95 in labor.

items.t: Harsh, delayed or erratic automatic shifting
items.job: Transmission software check, adaptive relearn and fluid change
items.note: RepairPal lists about $188-$217 for a fluid change. A rebuilt transmission costs thousands.

items.t: Timing belt wear and slipped timing
items.job: Replace timing belt and tensioner (often with water pump)
items.note: KBB lists about $409-$953 including labor. Engine repair after a broken belt costs far more.

items.t: Cranks but won't start (crank sensor or reluctor)
items.note: YourMechanic averages about $974 total, with higher quotes for the 3.5L.

items.job: Diagnose idle and throttle control; clean throttle body
items.note: One owner paid about $930 for sensors without fixing it, so ask for a firm diagnosis first.

items.t: Clunk or grinding from torn CV axle boots
items.note: About $150 for a boot; a worn CV joint or axle costs $500 or more.

items.t: A/C stops cooling on long drives
items.note: Diagnosis only, because the fix depends on what the shop finds (refrigerant charge, sensor or relay). YourMechanic averages $111 ($16 parts, $95 labor); shop/dealer $146–$198 by year.
